question: A restaurant's menu lists the dishes you can order. Why can the kitchen replace its stoves without telling any customer?
options: Customers depend only on what the menu promises, not on how the kitchen works
Customers never notice anything the kitchen does
New stoves always cook the same food faster
The kitchen prints a new menu every time it changes
explanation: The menu is the contract, like an API. As long as the dishes on it stay the same, everything behind it can change. Customers do notice when a dish is removed or changed, which is why breaking changes to an API need a new version.
